title: Vaginal Birth After Caesarean: Antenatal Counselling

evidenceAudit.scope: Pregnant woman with one or more previous caesarean births attending a Saudi antenatal clinic: who can be offered a planned vaginal birth after caesarean, contraindications, individual chance of success and risk of uterine rupture, comparison with elective repeat caesarean from 39 weeks, special circumstances, shared decision making and documentation, and the preparation for an elective repeat caesarean if chosen. Uses the Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists Green-top Guideline No. 45 and Saudi tertiary centre data; no Saudi national guideline was found.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-20.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi Ministry of Health or Saudi Society of Obstetrics and Gynecology guideline on birth after caesarean was found; the RCOG Green-top Guideline No. 45 (2015) is used and is a United Kingdom guideline. A newer edition may exist and the RCOG site could not be checked for an update.

The only Saudi data used are from one tertiary centre in Jeddah (1,139 women, 2011 to 2018, excluding induction, two or more caesareans, and estimated fetal weight over 4 kg); a vaginal birth rate of 72.9% in women with no earlier trial of labour is described but it is not national and should be replaced by the local unit's own audit figures as the guideline advises (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 7.3).

Antibiotic doses: the guideline names cefuroxime plus metronidazole before the skin incision; cefazolin 1 g (the dose on the US label for perioperative prophylaxis) is written because the cefazolin label was reviewed, and a higher 2 g dose is used in some units; check local policy.

Betamethasone 12 mg twice 12 to 24 hours apart is the dose used for fetal lung maturation in the placenta praevia topic from an NHS trust guideline; the guideline text read here cites a trial of prophylactic betamethasone before elective caesarean but did not give the dose, and the US label does not list obstetric use.
Thromboprophylaxis with low molecular weight heparin is required by the guideline but no label or regimen was reviewed, so none is written.
Sterilisation counselling at the time of caesarean is referred to but not written as a pathway.
The guideline's risk figures come from United Kingdom, United States and Australian studies done before 2015; they are not Saudi rates.
Figures were read by automated extraction of PDF and label text; spot-check each figure and dose against the source during clinical review.

pathophysiology.summary: A lower segment scar is weaker than normal womb muscle; labour can open it, with an overall risk of rupture of about 1 in 200 (0.5%) in planned vaginal birth (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 7.2). Uterine rupture risk is lowest in spontaneous labour (0.15 to 0.4%) and rises with induction (0.54 to 1.4%) and with oxytocin augmentation (0.9 to 1.91%) (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 7.2). A previous vaginal birth is the best predictor of success (85 to 90%) and also lowers rupture risk (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 7.4). Each repeat caesarean adds risk of placenta praevia, placenta accreta and adhesions in later pregnancies (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 6.2 and Section 7.2). The greatest chance of harm is when a planned vaginal birth ends in emergency caesarean (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 7.2). Babies born by elective caesarean before 39 weeks have more breathing problems (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 9.1).

symptoms: Pregnant woman with one or more earlier caesarean births asking how she should give birth (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 7.1).
Worry about pain, injury to the scar or having another operation (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 7.1).
Wish for several more children, which favours attempting vaginal birth (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 6.3).
Past labour problems such as slow progress or distress that led to the caesarean (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 7.4).
physicalSigns: Midline or transverse lower scar on the abdomen does not show the type of uterine incision; the operation note must be reviewed (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 6.1).
Body mass index over 30, age 40 or over, and a large baby lower the chance of success (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 7.4 and Section 10).
Fetal presentation and placental site on ultrasound (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 6.2).
Scar thickness over the amniotic cavity of 0.6 to 2.0 mm suggests a scar defect, but no cut-off is ready for routine use (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 6.4).
redFlags: Previous uterine rupture or classical caesarean scar: planned vaginal birth is contraindicated (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 6.2).
Major placenta praevia or any other absolute contraindication to vaginal birth: plan caesarean (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 6.2).
Low vertical or inverted T or J incision, or extension of the uterine incision: senior obstetrician decision (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 6.2).
Placenta praevia with a previous caesarean: assess for placenta accreta and plan a multidisciplinary delivery (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 9.1).
Two or more previous caesareans: counsel by a senior obstetrician and deliver in a centre with immediate surgery (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 6.3).
Unplanned labour or bleeding, pain or reduced fetal movements at any gestation: attend hospital at once (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 7.1 and Section 8.1).
precipitants: Induction of labour, no previous vaginal birth, body mass index over 30 and a previous caesarean for dystocia reduce the chance of success; if all are present success is about 40% (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 7.4).
Short interval of less than 12 months from the last birth, post-dates, age 40 or over, obesity, large baby and unfavourable cervix may raise rupture risk (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 6.4).
Previous uterine surgery such as myomectomy entering the cavity (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 6.2).
Twin pregnancy, post-dates or stillbirth: uncertain safety, careful approach (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 10).
Giving birth in a unit without immediate surgery and neonatal resuscitation (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Single previous lower segment caesarean, singleton cephalic baby at 37+0 weeks or more, no contraindication (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 6.1).

differentials.condition: Contraindicated: previous rupture or classical scar
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Documented uterine rupture or classical or high vertical incision in the operation note (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 6.2).
Low vertical, inverted T or J incision, large extension, two or more caesareans, myomectomy (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 6.2 and Section 6.3).
Placenta over or near the scar on the anomaly or third trimester scan; plan with the placenta praevia pathway (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 9.1).
Informed preference after counselling; involve an obstetrician and plan from 39+0 weeks (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 5.1 and Section 9.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Identify women with a previous caesarean
actions: Record the number and indication of earlier caesareans and obtain the operation notes (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 6.1).
Follow the routine antenatal schedule and add the specific reviews of the care pathway (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 5.1).
Use a birth-choices checklist or care pathway to guide counselling and documentation (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 5.1 and Section 7.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Check suitability
actions: Confirm single lower segment scar, singleton cephalic pregnancy and no contraindication (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 6.1).

Refer to an obstetrician if there is a contraindication, uncertainty, request for caesarean, need for induction or a complication such as pre-eclampsia, breech or growth restriction (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 5.1).
Assess factors that raise rupture risk and tailor the discussion (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 6.4).

clinicalManagement.title: Counsel on benefits and risks
actions: Explain that successful vaginal birth has the fewest complications and emergency caesarean after a trial of labour carries the greatest risk (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 7.2).
Quote a 72 to 75% chance of success, 85 to 90% with a previous vaginal birth, and about 1 in 200 uterine rupture risk (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 7.2 to Section 7.4).
Explain the extra risk with induction and oxytocin, and that perinatal death after planned vaginal birth is about 4 in 10,000 (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 7.2 and Section 8.2).
Explain repeat caesarean risks: longer recovery, placenta praevia and accreta in later pregnancies, adhesions, and breathing problems if before 39 weeks (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 7.2).
Give a patient information leaflet and ask about her wish for future children (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 7.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Agree and document the plan
actions: Agree the mode of birth with the woman and document it before the expected date (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 7.1).
If a caesarean is chosen, set the date from 39+0 weeks and document a plan for labour starting earlier (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 7.1 and Section 9.1).
If vaginal birth is chosen, plan birth in a unit with continuous monitoring, immediate caesarean and neonatal resuscitation (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).
Review at 41+0 weeks with a senior obstetrician if labour has not started (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 10).

clinicalManagement.title: Prepare elective repeat caesarean if chosen
actions: Give antibiotics before the skin incision (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 9.1).
Give thromboprophylaxis as in the RCOG guideline (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 9.1).
Avoid delivery before 39+0 weeks; discuss steroid risks if earlier birth is needed (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 9.1).
Use a multidisciplinary plan if placenta praevia is present (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 9.1).

regimens.indication: Prophylaxis against wound, urinary and womb infection before elective repeat caesarean
regimens.patientGroup: Women having elective repeat caesarean without cephalosporin allergy
regimens.dose: 1 g as a single dose 30 to 60 minutes before the skin incision (Cefazolin label, Perioperative Prophylactic Use); the guideline names cefuroxime with metronidazole as the preferred choice (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 9.1). Dilution and preparation: reconstitute each 1 g vial with 2.5 mL of sterile water for injection (about 330 mg/mL), shake well; for direct injection dilute further with about 5 mL of sterile water and inject slowly over 3 to 5 minutes; for infusion dilute in 50 to 100 mL of 0.9% sodium chloride or 5% dextrose (Cefazolin label, Reconstitution and Administration).
regimens.route: Intravenous injection over 3 to 5 minutes or intravenous infusion; the label also allows intramuscular use
regimens.duration: Single dose; repeat only if the operation lasts 2 hours or more (Cefazolin label, Perioperative Prophylactic Use)
adjustments: Give before the skin incision, not after cord clamping; this reduces infection more (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 9.1).
Do not use co-amoxiclav as prophylaxis before the incision because of a possible rise in necrotising enterocolitis in the baby (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 9.1).
Renal impairment: reduce the interval or dose for repeated dosing (Cefazolin label, Dosage).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Hypersensitivity during and after the injection (Cefazolin label, Warnings).
Diarrhoea after antibiotics may be Clostridioides difficile colitis (Cefazolin label, Warnings).
contraindications: Known allergy to the cephalosporin group of antibiotics (Cefazolin label, Contraindications).
regimens.sourceTitle: RCOG Green-top Guideline No. 45: Birth After Previous Caesarean Birth (October 2015)
regimens.sourceEdition: RCOG Green-top 45, Section 9.1; Cefazolin label, Perioperative Prophylactic Use and Reconstitution

regimens.indication: Anaerobic cover with the pre-incision antibiotic for elective repeat caesarean
regimens.dose: 500 mg as a single dose with the cephalosporin (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 9.1 names metronidazole with cefuroxime; dose from the Metronidazole label). Dilution and preparation: use the ready-made 500 mg per 100 mL isotonic solution; no dilution; do not use with aluminium needles.
regimens.route: Intravenous infusion over about one hour (Metronidazole label, Dosage and Administration)
adjustments: Take no alcohol during treatment because of a disulfiram-like reaction (Metronidazole label, Contraindications).
Severe liver disease: reduce the dose (Metronidazole label, Precautions).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Nausea, metallic taste and neurological symptoms with longer courses (Metronidazole label, Adverse Reactions).
Thrombophlebitis at the infusion site (Metronidazole label, Adverse Reactions).
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to metronidazole or other nitroimidazoles (Metronidazole label, Contraindications).
Disulfiram taken within the last 2 weeks (Metronidazole label, Contraindications).
regimens.sourceTitle: RCOG Green-top Guideline No. 45: Birth After Previous Caesarean Birth (October 2015)
regimens.sourceEdition: RCOG Green-top 45, Section 9.1; Metronidazole injection label, Contraindications and Dosage

regimens.indication: Reduce breathing problems in the baby when elective repeat caesarean is needed before 39+0 weeks (off-label)
regimens.patientGroup: Women needing elective repeat caesarean at 37+0 to 38+6 weeks
regimens.dose: 12 mg per dose, two doses given 12 to 24 hours apart (Celestone Soluspan holds 3 mg betamethasone as sodium phosphate plus 3 mg as acetate per mL, 6 mg total per mL, so 12 mg is 2 mL). Dilution and preparation: shake well before use; do not dilute and do not mix with preservative-containing diluents (parabens, phenol), which can cause flocculation.
regimens.route: Deep intramuscular injection; never intravenous and never epidural (Celestone Soluspan label, Warnings)
adjustments: Off-label: the Celestone Soluspan US label lists no obstetric use; the guideline cites a trial in which it halved breathing problems when elective caesarean was done after 37+0 weeks (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 9.1).

Counsel that a follow-up study found twice the rate of lowest school achievement in exposed children and that efforts should be to avoid delivery before 39+0 weeks rather than use steroids more freely (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 9.1).
Diabetes: monitor glucose closely and add insulin per local protocol (Celestone Soluspan label, Precautions).
Infants should be observed for signs of hypoadrenalism after maternal corticosteroids (Celestone label, Pregnancy).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Maternal blood glucose, especially in diabetes (Celestone Soluspan label, Precautions).
Signs of systemic infection or fungal infection (Celestone Soluspan label, Warnings).
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to any component of the product (Celestone Soluspan label, Contraindications).
Idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura (intramuscular route) (Celestone Soluspan label, Contraindications).
Systemic fungal infection unless needed to control a drug reaction (Celestone Soluspan label, Warnings).

medicationPlan.note: Counselling itself needs no medicine. The medicines below apply only if an elective repeat caesarean is chosen or planned before 39 weeks. The choice follows RCOG Green-top 45; doses, dilution, administration method and contraindications come from the product labels named in each row. All doses are for adult women. diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Singleton cephalic pregnancy at 37+0 weeks or more with a single previous lower segment caesarean (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 6.1).
Soon after the mid-trimester ultrasound; decision finalised by 36+0 weeks (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 5.1).
72 to 75% overall; 85 to 90% with a previous vaginal birth (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 7.3 and Section 7.4).

diagnosticCriteria.criterion: Risk of uterine rupture in planned vaginal birth
diagnosticCriteria.threshold: About 1 in 200 (0.5%); spontaneous labour 0.15 to 0.4%, induced 0.54 to 1.4%, augmented 0.9 to 1.91% (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 7.2).
At 41+0 weeks if spontaneous labour has not started (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 10).

values: 72 to 75% succeed; 85 to 90% with a previous vaginal birth (Section 7.3 and Section 7.4)

teaching.scope: Pregnant woman with one or more previous caesarean births attending a Saudi antenatal clinic: who can be offered a planned vaginal birth after caesarean, contraindications, individual chance of success and risk of uterine rupture, comparison with elective repeat caesarean from 39 weeks, special circumstances, shared decision making and documentation, and the preparation for an elective repeat caesarean if chosen. Uses the Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists Green-top Guideline No. 45 and Saudi tertiary centre data; no Saudi national guideline was found.
learningObjectives: Offer planned vaginal birth to most women with one previous lower segment caesarean and a singleton cephalic baby at 37+0 weeks or more.
Quote 72 to 75% success and about 1 in 200 rupture risk, and use local figures where available.
Finish the decision by 36+0 weeks, document it and give a leaflet.
If caesarean is chosen, operate from 39+0 weeks with antibiotics and thromboprophylaxis.
pitfalls: Not reading the previous operation note.
Using only published figures instead of local rates.
Not documenting the discussion and the plan if labour starts early.
keyPoints: Previous uterine rupture or classical scar contraindicates planned vaginal birth.
A previous vaginal birth is the best predictor of success.
Induction and oxytocin raise rupture risk two- to three-fold.

patientEducation: Most women with one earlier caesarean can try for a vaginal birth; about 3 in 4 succeed.
The chance is higher, about 9 in 10, if you have given birth vaginally before.
About 1 in 200 women have a tear of the scar in labour; this is why you should give birth in a hospital with an operating theatre.
A repeat caesarean avoids labour but has its own risks for this and future pregnancies.
Come to hospital at once with regular tightenings, waters breaking, bleeding or constant pain.
You can change your mind at any time; we will write your plan in your notes.
lifestyleAndDiet: Keep a healthy weight and stay active.
Wait at least 12 months after birth before the next pregnancy if you can.
Plan how you will get to the hospital quickly when labour starts.
Bring your previous operation report if you were seen elsewhere.
mdtReferrals: Obstetrician and gynaecologist; midwife; family physician; anaesthetist; sonographer; neonatologist; pharmacist.
dischargeCriteria: Counselling documented with the chance of success and the risks; plan for mode of birth agreed by 36+0 weeks; leaflet given; plan if labour starts before an elective caesarean date; place of birth confirmed.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Counsel after the mid-trimester scan; confirm the plan by 36+0 weeks; review at 41+0 weeks with a senior obstetrician if labour has not started; review the plan again whenever a complication arises.
